name: Semantic Anchor Extremes

name: Representation Robustness as Physical Privilege Failure
notes: Fine and coarse record maps can both be representation robust while inducing different distinguishability partitions; robustness is not physical privilege.

name: Empirical Interface as Response Law Failure
notes: Primitive allowed-response relations, response distributions, or complete possibility sets smuggle substantive physical selection into semantics under strong PGH.

name: Arbitrary or Response-Sensitive Interface Closure
notes: Arbitrary closure operators and freely chosen constructor families universally encode target interfaces; response-sensitive closure imports substantive physics.

name: Unique or Minimal Empirical Seed

name: Generic Empirical Substructure Privilege Selectors
notes: No tested general intrinsic selector avoids nonuniqueness, trivial extremes, or extra selector input; special asymmetric grammar uniqueness remains possible.

name: Residual Strong PGH R1 Unsatisfied
notes: The original residual target's physically justified irrelevance-selector burden remains unmet at current scope; an anchored successor is explicit rather than a retroactive success claim.

name: Current Grammar R2 Law Exhaustion Failure

name: Unprivileged Local-to-Global Input Selection

name: Generated Cover Compatibility Schema

name: Free Local Assignment Gluing

name: Local Admissibility Support Origin Failure

name: Local Admissibility Generator Family Map

name: Finite Local Predicate Universal Encoding

name: Unrestricted Support Description Language Failure
notes: Unrestricted predicates and unprivileged description languages can encode arbitrary supports; compactness alone does not establish generated necessity.
